important_discovery.existing_grain: one row per geography x reference_month x dwelling_type (tall/narrow — dwelling_type is a row discriminator, not a column set)
important_discovery.existing_constraints: no unique constraint exists yet — only two non-unique indexes (geography_id/reference_month/dwelling_type, state_code/reference_month)
important_discovery.sprint9_required_grain: one WIDE row per geography (Phase 4 spec explicitly: 'Prefer one wide row per geography instead of a large tall fact table'), with dwelling-type-specific medians as separate COLUMNS (e.g. median_sale_price_detached, median_sale_price_apartment) rather than separate rows
important_discovery.decision: Extend these existing tables additively in migration 013 (ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS for every new field the Sprint 9 spec requires, plus a NEW expression-based unique index on geography_id for the wide-row grain). Do not create differently-named replacement tables — that would duplicate an already-declared, never-populated placeholder and add confusion. The legacy dwelling_type/median_sale_price/median_rent/gross_yield/population_growth_1y/dwelling_approvals_12m columns are kept for backward compatibility (documented as superseded by the new per-type columns) since dropping/renaming columns would be destructive and no code depends on them either way.
important_discovery.safety: Confirmed via grep across the whole repo (excluding node_modules): zero references to either table name outside supabase/migrations/003_warehouse_foundation.sql. Safe to extend.

nsw_sales_dwelling_classification_audit.current_classification_gap: 2,556,681 rows (the entire 'detached_house' bucket) are assigned purely from (nature_of_property='RESIDENCE', zone_code='R', strata_lot IS NULL) with no further distinction. Of these, 18,617 rows have a non-null unit_number and 95 rows have a '/' in house_number while still being non-strata — the standard NSW torrens-title signal for a subdivided villa/townhouse/duplex development that was never strata-titled (e.g. multiple sale records at the same street address with unit_number 1..6, confirmed by direct sample inspection: '14 East Cres' has 6 distinct unit_number values, clearly a multi-dwelling torrens development, not one detached house).
nsw_sales_dwelling_classification_audit.evidence_based_new_rule_identified: RESIDENCE + zone R + strata_lot NULL + (unit_number NOT NULL OR house_number contains '/') => townhouse_villa_semidetached (medium confidence, deterministic, no price/suburb/postcode inference). Affects 18,712 of 2,556,681 currently-detached_house rows (0.73%) — a real but modest reclassification, exactly the kind of narrow evidence-supported improvement the sprint asks for rather than an invented broad heuristic.
nsw_sales_dwelling_classification_audit.duplex_scoping_decision: PSI source data has no field that cleanly separates 'duplex' from other torrens-titled multi-dwelling forms (townhouse/villa/semi) — a duplex-specific rule would require inferring from lot-count or price, which is explicitly forbidden. Sprint 9 will NOT introduce a distinct duplex bucket; the villa/townhouse/semi evidence above covers duplexes too, documented explicitly in the classification doc rather than inventing an unsupported split.

risks_and_implementation_decisions: Branch already has two never-populated placeholder mart tables with a narrower grain than Sprint 9 needs — resolved by additive ALTER TABLE extension, not replacement (see important_discovery above).

RLS is disabled branch-wide but currently unreachable (no client points at the branch) — Sprint 9 Phase 9 adds a minimal, tested public view/RPC layer rather than retrofitting RLS across 35 existing tables (out of this sprint's scope; documented as a follow-up).

The app's existing Supabase client/env-var pattern is production-only — a new, separate server-only warehouse client with its own env vars is required so the branch is never reachable from the production app config.
An existing, unrelated /suburb-intelligence route exists — the new feature must use a different route (/research) to avoid collision or the appearance of replacing a shipped feature.
Do not proceed with production writes at any point — confirmed production has zero warehouse schemas; this must be re-verified after every branch load.
